claims.statement: The consolidated Electricity Directive provides for frameworks for flexible connection agreements where network capacity is limited or unavailable.
A flexible connection can specify firm and flexible injection or withdrawal capacity, charges and duration, but remains a DSO agreement rather than a freely transferable asset.

contrary_evidence: EU rules support flexible-connection frameworks but do not prove Polish implementation, site-option transferability or developer willingness to pay.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: source sites through electrical contractors, renewable installers, commercial-property managers and the family company's regional relationships.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: validate 10 options in year 1, transfer 12 projects annually by year 3, build 3 million PLN of retained cash and option value by year 5, and reach 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 7-10.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day with engineering and legal diligence outsourced.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 45%-70% gross margin after option payments, engineering screens, legal review and failed-site write-offs.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 18-30 months because most early sites may fail technical or legal diligence.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 40,000-150,000 PLN development fee per transferred site option plus a 1%-3% project revenue interest.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: property managers and developers repeat across portfolios; no repeat rate is established.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Each DSO response and site outcome improves the private model of which physical and contractual site features survive diligence
fingerprint.customer: Battery, charging and flexible-load developers that need controllable sites with plausible grid access
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Property-owner sourcing through installers and property managers; developer demand through repeat portfolio agreements
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Exclusive site control plus a standardised technical and contractual dossier, sold for a development fee and residual interest
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A developer pays when it acquires or exercises a qualified site option
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A developer pipeline is blocked by slow site control and connection diligence

founder_fit: Uses family-business access to energy sites and contractors.
Rewards analytical screening rather than constant social selling.
Capital can be staged through conditional options.
risks: A land option may not convey any grid advantage.
Concentration in one DSO region could create long delays.

structure.control_point: Long-dated conditional site options and owner-authorised access to meter, load and connection documentation
structure.critical_dependency: DSO approval, enforceable land contracts and project-specific confirmation that the proposed use can connect

thesis: Secure conditional, exclusive lease or development options over Polish commercial sites with useful existing electrical infrastructure, then package land control, load data and a DSO-tested flexible-connection pathway for storage and high-power-load developers. The defensible asset is a bank of site rights and verified connection dossiers, not a public map or an attempt to resell grid capacity itself.
title: Flexible-Grid Site Option Bank
uncertainties: Polish DSO implementation of flexible connections
Permitted assignment structure for project options
